featured_reviews.name: Niyati Singhvi
featured_reviews.review_text: This place stands out with its unconventional concept of combining a library and café, creating a cozy and relaxed vibe that’s perfect for unwinding. It’s easy to locate and has a warm, inviting atmosphere. The Nutella melted pancakes are a highlight—not just delicious but also creatively presented in cute shapes. The Malta Mojito is refreshing, and the Café Bonbon is definitely worth trying. The toasted garlic bread, however, is skippable. The space isn’t ideal for large groups, but it’s a great spot for a quick outing. Overall, definitely recommended for a visit.

featured_reviews.name: D M
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I were to rate the cafe's concept, it would be a 5! But if you ask me about my overall experience, it will be strictly a 3.

The ambience is bang on perfect for hanging out with friends. There are books stacked like a mini library which you can read while you enjoy a bite. The food that we tried was so not great though. We tried:

•White sauce chicken pasta
•Chicken B2BLC sandwich
•Cold coffee with almond milk (of which the almond milk quantity was only available for 1 serve. Disappointing.)
•Cold coffee with hazelnut
•Paneer pesto crepe
•Chicken fingers

Overall, the pasta was the winner. It was cooked very well with the sauce tasting creamy and delicious. It was served with the normal bread cut into triangles and toasted. The sandwich size was quite huge with a good amount of filling. Not at all a fan of both the cold coffees - One with almond milk and the other with cow milk. The paneer pesto wrap didn’t have salt and the taste was quite off and not balanced. It’s supposed to be creamy but instead we could taste only the greens. It was a total letdown. The crepe covering was nice though but again what’s the point? Chicken fingers seemed a bit over-fried and stale served with a sauce (it was definitely not mayonnaise as told to us) which did not go well. We chose not to eat all 6 pieces as a result.

The service was alright. The server made a face when we could not finish everything on the plate and commented that it would be given to someone else. Now I understand that’s very noble of them to do that to prevent food wastage. I politely replied on the same lines with a smile. His tone seemed rude nor were there any other mannerisms leaving us baffled and uncomfortable.

Overall not a great experience and would skip returning.

featured_reviews.name: Prajakta Chorge
featured_reviews.review_text: The staff members are very welcoming. I enjoyed the cafe bonbon; it is quite good if you appreciate a strong coffee. I truly love both the place and its ambiance. I would highly recommend it for meeting with friends and it's also a wonderful spot for book lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Pranay Hegde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay to Barcelona is a must-visit café if you’re in Mumbai!
The food here is amazing and the vibe is just perfect. Absolutely loved the paneer pesto sandwich and the coffees are really good too .
But the best thing above all? The staff and their service—truly top knotch.
If you’re here, don’t miss reading about the team and the owner who are building this beautiful place. Their story makes the experience even more special.

featured_reviews.name: Avi Kadu
featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all, gratitude to the owner for working towards the development of the society. I have also read your personal journey, and it is truly inspiring to see where you started and what you have built today.
However, I would like to share my honest feedback about the food quality and service, which was disappointing during our visit.
I ordered a coffee, but it was not hot. I finished it quietly without creating any issue; you may even check the CCTV if required. However, proper serving temperature should be ensured.
We ordered a chicken omelette with cheese, but honestly, it was difficult to find the chicken in it. Initially, I thought there might be chunks inside, but there were no visible shreds or proper quantity. That was quite disappointing.
We also ordered nachni pancakes, and the dish was served with cold caramel sauce that seemed straight from the fridge.
Ideally, the server should inform whether the sauce will be served on the side or on top. Warm pancakes with apple and caramel sauce should not be cold, as it completely spoils the taste of the dish.
When the bill came, the lady at the counter suggested we need not pay due to the experience. However, we respect your effort and the noble work you are doing, so we chose to pay.
Sir, basic training for the chef and kitchen team is necessary. My child is autistic, and after waiting patiently for quite some time, receiving such food was disappointing for us. Eventually, we left the place dissatisfied.
I must mention that the server was good and well-trained, but he was slightly pushy while promoting initiatives. Sometimes this can irritate guests, so a balanced approach would help.
Please understand that we are genuine food lovers and not here to damage anyone’s reputation. We appreciate your noble work and truly hope you continue doing it. Just focus a little more on food quality, serving standards, and taste, and the place can become even better.
✅ Suggested Next Step:
If you want, I can also create a shorter, sharper Google review (more impactful and slightly aggressive) which usually gets faster attention from restaurant management.

featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! The ambience is calm, welcoming, and has a beautiful vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease. I tried the Pink Sauce Pasta and the Spanish Omelette—the food was really good and well-prepared.

The service was handled by Jyoti (I hope I’ve got the name right—referring to the tall girl who also models), and she was excellent throughout. There was a small glitch in service because of which we couldn’t fully enjoy the Spanish Omelette, but Kushboo handled the feedback very gracefully. The way she spoke about the café’s story and its origin was truly inspiring.

It’s not just a café—it’s a place with a heart. Definitely worth visiting, especially to hear the story from Kushboo herself.

I’m giving one star less only because there’s room for improvement in the service, which I’m sure can be fixed with a little bit of training.

featured_reviews.name: Harshad Dhamankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have visited lot of times. Below contains reviews ans pictures taken multiple times.
Holi - The festival of colors. The same resembles to the food we eat. On this festive fervor, I stepped in to enjoy this magnificent colorful Holi Brunch.
As soon as you stepped @courtyardmumbai you will see huge dessert counter. But today my eyes captured all authentic glossy, classy, looking desserts and I was so amazed. Everything was looking stunningly colorful.
I started my Brunch with Khow Suey and varieties of starters. I love the Ragda Patis Chaat, Chhole Kulche, specially Chhole was made up with nice Punjabi style. Litti Choka was absolutely delicious. The sourness, spiciness and hint gave the perfect tongue twister. Potato Cheese balls were crispy and went well with green chatni. Ditto with Paneer, mashroom and babycorn Satay.
In main course I had various varieties amongst that Hyderabadi Biryani was delicious. Curd was not at all sour. The vegetables cooked with appropriate spices. Paneer Lababdar was definitely winner here.
Now my favorite part during the Brunch which, was Dessert. As I said I couldn't refrain myself from eating desserts at the earliest. I again selected Indian desserts and it was WOW!. Each and every dessert was made in uniquely. Different types of Gujiyas, Meetha Samosa were so delicious ditto with Jalebi and Laddu which was packed with lot of Ghee. The Coconut Rasgulla won my heart too. Meetha Paan was stuffed with dry fruits and had a Gulkand flavor to it. Very rare I see this unique dessert. I wish there couldn't have been any disease called Diabetes to repeat all those desserts multiple times. 😅
To accompany my meal I had Pina Colada (complimentary given) and Fresh Lime Soda. I had those to bring my taste buds back from the colorful food.
Service was great and I never had any complaints about service here. Everyone is on the tows ensuring there shouldn't be any delay.
So, I had a great Holi themed Brunch. Varieties of food but massive traditional dessert preparations bought more colors on my Brunch.

Dinner Time! I love dinner on weekend specially on Saturday that gives ample time to relax and eat everything on the table. And if I have such an amazing spread like this which offered @courtyardmumbai then it should be an elevating experience.
Starting from soup till the dessert I couldn't found even a single dish that was lacking spice.
Starting with soup and starter, this time Tomato Shorba was not thick but had spice to it. Chat platter was delicious and the curd used was not at all sour. Rest starters were good how ever I didn't eat Paneer Tikka more cos I had to save space for later course. 😅
I loved Punjabi Kadhi though gave a perfect spice along with aloo palak dry sabji. Veg Dum Biryani was packed with lot of flavors and for me it was spicy but the taste can be managed by adding curd. I didn't ordered roti this time I finished everything with plain rice and Biryani.
How can I miss desserts. I specially saved some space to grab those desserts. Balushai was so amazing ditto with Bengali sweet which topped with pomegranate and chocolate cream and dry fruits. Western desserts were good but I love the Indian desserts more.
At last I had fresh lime water to wash it down again it was not sour and bitter. Was rightly made balancing sweetness.
Alright, I enjoyed the dinner but being honest what I enjoyed more was main course and Desserts.
Service was excellent and I never waited so long to get the dish on the table. I never had service issues @courtyardmumbai which made my overall experience more delightful. No doubt

featured_reviews.review_text:
A charming little spot with proper coffee and big heart.

Lokoman Café isn't a trendy, flashy destination—it's a small, warm, and genuinely friendly neighbourhood spot where the focus is clearly on good coffee, simple homemade food, and a welcoming vibe.

The Atmosphere (5/5):
We loved the feel of it. It's compact and cozy, with a rustic, slightly vintage decor. Mismatched furniture, local art on the walls, and shelves with books and board games give it a real "living room" feel. There's a small, sunny terrace perfect for people-watching. The music was low-key, and the overall noise level lets you actually have a conversation.

Coffee & Food (4/5):
The coffee is the real deal. We had a flat white and a pour-over—both were expertly made, smooth, and rich. They clearly know their beans. We tried the "Lokoman Breakfast Plate" (eggs, sourdough, avocado, halloumi) and the Banana Bread. The food is fresh, wholesome, and tastes homemade. Portions are generous without being overwhelming. The banana bread, warm and moist, was a standout.

Service & Vibe:
The owner or manager (we assume) was behind the bar, and the service was exceptionally warm and personal. You get the sense this is a passion project, not a chain. It feels like a community hub; several patrons seemed to be regulars, greeted by name.

Things to Note:

It's small. On a busy weekend, you might wait for a table inside, but turnover seems reasonable.

The menu is compact—think all-day breakfast, sandwiches, salads, cakes, and stellar coffee. Don't expect a vast, sprawling menu.

It’s a place for slowing down. Perfect for a quiet catch-up, some reading, or getting a bit of work done in a pleasant environment.

Final Take:
Lokoman Café is a gem for those tired of impersonal, overpriced coffee shops. It’s authentic, unpretentious, and delivers exactly what it promises: excellent coffee, tasty comfort food, and a cozy atmosphere served with a sincere smile. We left feeling happily caffeinated and already planning our next visit. A wonderful local find.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an absolutely fantastic experience at the restaurant. It was a last minute decision to visit cafe crema for a weekday night dinner and we left the restaurant happy. The restaurant has both buffet and alacarte. The buffet spread was moderate but all the dishes were really well made with great flavors.
The bean curd soup served had many green vegetables and a flavorful broth. The salads were also delicious with some spicy (sprout salad) and peppery (corn salad) options. The additional make your salad desk with sauteed zucchini,herbed capsicum were all fresh and tasted good. Dhokla, the red & green chutneys for accompaniments were also delicious along with curd raita dips presented. The cheese and nuts platter looked promising but we moved on to the starters.
Paneer tikka, a veg kebab were offered in vegetarian selection. The paneer was harder and dry in tikka and the kebab was comparatively salty and oily. Hence we didn't enjoy their appetizers much.

In the main course, chilly basil noodles and the asian gravy (cannot remember the name) were extremely delicious with a good chilly and basil flavor in the soft noodles. The cauliflower au gratin (cauliflower in white/yellow sauce) was also scrumptious and warm. In the Indian selection, paneer gravy curry, veg jalfrezi, dal and rice were hearty. Rice was surprisingl soft unlike the rice that gets hardened with over heating in most other buffets. We had roti/naam to choose from and the wheat roti was soft and promptly served upon order.
Desserts also impressed us with the quality inspite of a limited variety. Malpua was thick soft and had saunf that gave a good start to the desserts. Chocolate pudding, a couple of other cakes in strawberry & Nutella flavors, a banana drycl cake and a sugar free cake were offered. The dry fruit chikki was an unusual dessert offering but we loved their choice to include good desserts that don't harm the appetite.
We had also ordered their truffle parmesan fries for our kid from the alacarte menu which took a really long time to be served but was fresh and homemade.

There were no baby chairs/booster seats to enable toddlers or young kids to have their meal comfortably though. Staff were kind enough to help add additional cushions on the chair to allow our kid to dine comfortably.

It was valet parking to park the vehicle while visiting this restaurant.

Desserts & Drinks
The dessert spread was impressive, featuring various cakes, halwa, and a rich chocolate pudding. My only critique here is that adding a scoop of ice cream would have made the experience perfect.
Why 4 Stars? The only reason I’m docking one star is that no soft drinks or lassi or chaas are included in the buffet spread, which felt like a missed opportunity.
Bonus Tip:

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Paradise offers a pleasant ambiance with good service, including options for AC and non-AC seating as well as a family hall, making it a convenient choice for different group types. The staff are courteous and attentive, contributing to a positive dining experience. However, there are notable concerns about the food quality, particularly with the egg fried rice, which did not meet expectations.

The egg fried rice ordered contained chicken, which was unexpected and suggests either a mistake or a less conventional preparation. In authentic Chinese cuisine, egg fried rice usually does not include meat unless specified. Moreover, the use of spices like cardamom and cinnamon in the fried rice is unusual for traditional Chinese recipes. These spices are more commonly found in South Asian dishes like biryanis and can result in a dry texture and flavor profile that is quite different from the typical savory and umami taste expected from Chinese fried rice. This deviation likely contributed to the dissatisfaction with the dish.

Additionally, the drink options were limited. The Goli soda offered, while a unique choice, had an inconvenient cap design that made drinking awkward, detracting further from the overall dining experience.

To summarize, while the ambiance and service at Cafe Paradise are commendable—with comfortable seating and friendly staff—the food quality, specifically the egg fried rice, could be improved to better align with authentic Chinese flavors. The unusual use of spices like cardamom and cinnamon, along with the unexpected chicken addition, resulted in a dish that was dry and lacked the typical taste profile. The drink selection also needs enhancement for a better customer experience. Improvements in menu authenticity and drink variety could make Cafe Paradise a more satisfying dining destination

We wanted tousing one table for our food and another for playing games, and despite explaining that we are regular customers and that the café had plenty of empty seating, she insisted we sit according to her preference. Ambiance

Value for Money

Overall Experience

I had the worst experience at the Versova Third Wave outlet.

I paid the bill, but their machine did not generate the payment slip. The payment status showed as completed, and the amount was deducted from my account. However, they told us that the payment was not received and that it might get reverted within a few minutes.

We had our meal, and while leaving, we again confirmed whether they had received the payment or not. Their team said they still hadn’t received it and asked us to pay again if we were leaving. They assured us that if the amount did not get reverted within 24 hours, they would provide a meal worth the same amount since the issue was from their end.

We agreed, paid again, and left.

We waited for 24 hours, but nothing happened. When we contacted them, they asked us to wait for 7 days. We waited for 10 days and revisited the place, but their behavior had completely changed and was very nonchalant.

They asked us to bring a printed bank statement from that day until the current date. I have one question: if the payment was completed to their bank, can’t they check the status from their end? If there are trust issues, that should be handled internally.

Another thing is that for ₹738, sharing my full transaction history and detailed bank statement with a café felt excessive. I’ve made some critical and large transactions from that account, and I’m uncomfortable sharing personal financial details.

One more point I want to mention: while we were placing the order and making the payment, another customer was in a hurry. The person taking orders processed her payment immediately after ours, and both transactions were handled in parallel. I believe this issue happened due to poor management.

That café is not close to my place, and traveling there again just to check the payment status is not worth it.

The owner mentioned that this is a very generic issue and has happened with other customers earlier. This does not sound acceptable. If this is a known issue, they should fix it instead of letting customers suffer.

Avoid this place if you can.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Prasad Kamble
featured_reviews.review_text:

Choco Caramel Latte – This one was a winner. The balance between chocolate, caramel, and coffee was spot on. It had a smooth texture and wasn’t too sugary, making it a great choice for those who enjoy a well-balanced flavored coffee.

Choco Hazelnut Frappe – If you love Nutella-like flavors, this frappe won’t disappoint. It was indulgent, chocolatey, and had a good hazelnut kick. The texture was creamy, and it wasn’t overly icy.

The ambiance of Third Wave Coffee was cozy, making it a great place to sit and relax. Service was quick and friendly. Overall, a good experience, and we’d definitely return to try more!

featured_reviews.name: Udit Khurana
featured_reviews.review_text:
Silk Road Coffee has slowly become my go to place in Versova, both to relax and to get some work done.

The coffee here is consistently great. I am usually not a fan of cold coffees, but their Vietnamese coffee was exceptionally well balanced and genuinely enjoyable.

They have a diverse range of food options, from lighter fresh options to more indulgent ones. The tiramisu french toast is amazing and definitely worth trying. Another thing I love is that they bake their breads fresh, which really shows in the quality of the food.

And the croissants absolutely deserve a special mention. They proudly say, “Who needs Paris when you have Silk Road for croissants,” and honestly, coming from someone who has actually spent time trying croissants across Paris, they are not wrong. Probably the best croissant I have had.

I also love the small cookies they serve alongside the coffee, a small touch that adds a lot to the experience.

The only small issue is that the common cushion seating could use a bit more regular cleaning.

Overall, a wonderful café with great coffee, comforting food, and an atmosphere that makes you want to keep coming back.

featured_reviews.name: Kanchan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fantastic place. Serene environment. Mind blowing bakery. This place is tucked away in a quiet lane in Versova and you step into a calm, relaxing place surrounded by trees and birds. A true rarity in the bustling city.
Coming to the point of the place: coffee… awesome flavors and options. Had the Vietnamese iced and it was fabulous. In addition to coffees, they also serve some refreshers and the tepache was so good that it was a no-brainer re-order. The food is also super quality… had the burrata sandwich, marinara sandwich, and the avocado salad and all of them were delectable. The bakery items are simply out of the world. Nothing compares to the croissant and pain au chocolate - do not miss (if it isn’t out of stock that is). Overall a fantastic place and btw saw a bunch of people working here as well - given the quietness around it seems like a perfect place to deal with your pesky boss or client 😉
